accuracy.evidence: Symbols checked against BBC Bitesize KS2 circuit symbols and the IEC 60617 / BS EN 60617 forms used in UK schools: cell as long thin (positive) and short thick lines, battery as two or more joined cells, lamp as a circle with a diagonal cross, switch as a hinged break (lifted open, flat closed), buzzer as a dome, wires as straight lines with square corners. NC Year 6 wording checked: recognised symbols, brightness and volume with number and voltage of cells, on/off switch positions. Two cells lighting the same lamp brighter is the Year 6 statement.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets known KS2 electricity errors (Bitesize and primary science misconception lists): 'open switch means on' (switch prediction, p2, tag open), drawing pictures instead of symbols (symbols prediction), mixing cell and lamp symbols (tag mix, m1), curly wires in diagrams (match prediction, tag real), switch position mattering in a single loop (draw prediction, m7, tag place), and a gap elsewhere not mattering (m8, tag gap).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcdiag draws real standard symbols on canvas and asks the child to read and write them: five symbol tiles to match by name, a loop with a dashed gap that a dragged wire closes, a tappable hinged switch that lights the lamp, a three-slot loop where tapping cycles symbols until cell + closed switch + buzzer is drawn, and a curly-wired real circuit matched to one of three mini diagrams. flagseries and flagcond use component words and material testing, not symbols.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds out by doing: picking the wrong tile names that tile's shape; the lamp only glows once the wire is in the gap; flipping the switch shows the lifted line as off; choosing an open switch in the draw task gives 'Nearly: that switch is open'; choosing diagram C names the open switch and diagram B the wrong cell count and lamp. The text then confirms.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions each with a tempting wrong option: a lamp symbol as 'a drawing of a glass bulb', a gapped circuit lighting because 'the cell still pushes', an open switch being on 'because open lets electricity through', the switch having to sit 'next to the + end of the cell', and real curly wires being drawn curly. The reveal names the pick after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (cell symbol, open switch, circle with a cross, how wires are drawn, two cells vs one, a gap by the lamp, switch position). Each wrong option has a tag with a specific message: mix (shape-to-name), open (open means off), real (straight lines), cells (more cells, brighter), gap (any gap breaks the loop), place (switch position in one loop).

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK combined 1.7 (paragraphs 0.5 to 3.2) and adult 4.8, well inside the family targets of 5.0 and 10.0. Component and symbol words (cell, battery, lamp, switch, buzzer, open, closed, complete circuit) each come with a plain description of the shape.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what a diagram is; each symbol's shape; open vs closed switch; complete loop and straight wires. Adult paragraphs: Year 6 and Year 4 links, standard symbol forms, six named mistakes and the lab steps. No filler pattern matched and the explanation overlap gate passed.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light: five symbol tiles sit in a two-column grid with labels, the loop fits with 34 px margins, the lit lamp glow and rays stay inside the canvas, slot labels sit above the top wire, and the three mini diagrams fit side by side at 358 px. Feedback wraps to three lines, and the buttons below are 48 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap or drag has a button twin: one button per symbol described by its shape, 'Put a wire in the gap', 'Close/Open the switch', 'Slot n: … → next' with the current symbol in aria-label, and 'Diagram A/B/C' with the parts read out. The canvas aria-label and live region carry every message. The walk gate passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
